events.title: von Neumann stored-program architecture
events.summary: John [von Neumann]'s 1945 'First Draft' report described [stored-program] computers — program and data in shared memory.
events.about: The [von Neumann] architecture still defines how CPUs fetch instructions from [RAM]. Every C program, [Python] interpreter, and JavaScript engine runs on this model unless explicitly heterogeneous (GPUs, TPUs).

narrative.whyChosen: [Stored-program] architecture is the blueprint of all general-purpose computers.
narrative.whyImportant: It unified programs and data in addressable memory.
narrative.problemSolved: Early computers rewired hardware to change programs; storage needed to be electronic and mutable.
